reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a technical tutorial and demonstration of Polygon or MATIC flash-loan arbitrage, with explanatory DeFi material and educational-purpose wording. The unusually large return claims and steps involving a contract are apparent promotional cues, but the available video evidence does not establish deception, actual profit, or a viewer outcome. The speaker's decoy-token statement is technical context whose effectiveness and relationship to any viewer solicitation remain unverified.

opening.argument: The promised return is directly tied to following and funding the demonstrated flash-loan workflow. The material advertises making thousands to millions daily through an “easy process,” then walks viewers through deploying a contract, sending MATIC to it, and initiating the flash loan. The speaker specifically says to send 131 MATIC and subsequently reports 936 MATIC. That is not merely general discussion of arbitrage: it links a substantial asset transfer and contract interaction to a much larger claimed return, which is the defining structure of a trading-bot or funded-contract solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not remove the solicitation. The description connects an “easy method” to daily earnings, supplies smart-contract and video links, and tells viewers to increase the gas fee to earn more. The on-screen procedure is also not abstract: it includes sending MATIC to a contract and running the flash loan. Those concrete instructions and the reported larger balance make the financial inducement central, even if the material does not independently prove the displayed result.

opening.argument: Several unusually strong warning signals appear together: cryptocurrency, a claimed daily return ranging from hundreds to millions, an “easy” method, external code and tutorial links, and instructions to increase the gas fee for a larger result. The description also warns that the method does not work on testnets and that tokens sent there will lose their value, pushing the viewer toward the real network. The video then shows a contract deployment and wallet interaction before presenting 936 MATIC. Taken together, this is a high-risk funded-contract return pitch, not a neutral explanation of DeFi concepts.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The relevant combination is an easy, extraordinary return claim plus external executable resources, a gas-fee instruction, and a real-network transaction workflow. Explaining what flash loans are does not neutralize those cues; it makes the pitch actionable. The fact that deception is not independently proven is not a reason to disregard the unusually strong risk pattern actually presented.

Even the warning about testnets can be read as an operational limitation of the claimed arbitrage process, not proof that the real-network method deceives users.
